title: Visual acceptance on Pi (the perceptual gate that lifts the block)
summary: Turn Pi's fail-closed visual-required block into a real verdict: judge the rendered app against its design with a vision-capable gate child grounded in the structured diff, and lift the block only on a genuine pass. This is the sole future work the shipped block-unrun-visual contract permits to replace that block.
motivation: Binder pi-visual-capture built the capture pipeline and evidence but deliberately left the block up; this binder adds the perceptual judgement that finally makes visual oracles pass or fail on Pi.

included: a new package-owned read-only visual gate role, projected across runtimes exactly as the other gate agents are, with the role-identity widening carried type-only through every closed union it feeds

a runner that attaches the app and design screenshots to a vision-capable gate child grounded in the structured diff and returns a verdict bound to the exact pixel bytes, with a vision-capability preflight that fail-closes when the gate model has no image input

wiring capture and the visual gate into verification so a visual oracle runs them after safety, and lifting the visual-required block only on a genuine pass while staying fail-closed at every unmet precondition
excluded: automatic provider fallback or model routing to find a vision-capable model — v1 gates on the configured gate model and blocks fail-closed when it has no image input; auto-routing is a later binder
changing the capture pipeline, env-server lifecycle, visual_env schema, or the structured diff shipped by pi-visual-capture
the Claude Code and Codex visual path (karta-validate), which is unchanged

design_facts.stack: TypeScript/Node Pi extension adding a vision-capable gate child (the proven amorphic image-attachment path) on top of the pi-visual-capture evidence artifact, structured diff, and env-server lifecycle

work_items.title: Define the read-only visual gate role and project it
work_items.summary: Add the vision reviewer as a package-owned read-only gate role, carry the role-identity widening type-only through every closed union it feeds, and project it across runtimes — no runner yet, so the block stays up.
work_items.contract: Add a package-owned, read-only visual gate role parallel to the acceptance and safety gates. Create the agent prompt agents/karta-design-reviewer.md (frontmatter name karta-design-reviewer), a role-catalog entry visual-gate (authority read-only, capabilities evidence.read, outputSchema gate-verdict-v1), and add karta-design-reviewer -> karta-verify to the BUNDLE_SITE map in scripts/sync_codex_agents.py so the agent projects to .codex/agents/karta-design-reviewer.toml and the bundled gate reference under skills/karta-verify/references/, with the .agents/ and plugins/karta/ mirrors following; keep every projection generated, never hand-authored, so validate_plugin and both projection --checks stay green. Adding the role widens the role identity, which ripples TYPE-ONLY through the closed unions it feeds and which must all be widened together for the package to typecheck: KartaRoleId (role-catalog.ts), KartaGateRoleId (capability-profile.ts), LifecycleRole (lifecycle-registry.ts, so a gate child of this role can be registered), the karta_dispatch role descriptions (dispatch-tool.ts), and the gate-test type signatures in tests/pi/verification-runner.test.ts and tests/pi/dispatch-tool.test.ts. In capability-profile.ts, map the visual-gate role to its declared read-only evidence tool rather than falling through to the boundary tool. All of these are type-only widenings: the visual gate is not wired, verification-runner.ts is untouched, and the pi-visual-capture block-holds assertions are unchanged. The prompt directs a vision-capable reviewer to judge a rendered app screenshot against its design screenshot, grounded in the structured discrepancies, and return a strict gate-verdict-v1 (pass, concerns, or blocked with findings).

signals: adds a new authority role (a gate) and widens several closed role/lifecycle unions type-only
edits the agent-projection generator (BUNDLE_SITE) and adds cross-runtime projections

the visual-gate role is read-only with no mutation or command capability, exactly like the acceptance and safety gate roles

the role-identity widening is carried type-only through KartaRoleId, KartaGateRoleId, LifecycleRole, the karta_dispatch role descriptions, and the gate-test signatures, so npm run check:pi (typecheck then tests) is green; verification-runner.ts is untouched and the pi-visual-capture block-holds assertions are unchanged

work_items.title: Judge the render against the design, bound to the pixel bytes
work_items.summary: Add the runner that attaches the screenshots to a vision-capable gate child, grounds it in the structured diff, and returns a verdict bound to the exact image bytes — with a vision preflight and a browserless floor.
work_items.contract: Add extensions/pi/visual-gate-runner.ts that judges a pi-visual-capture karta-visual-evidence-v1 artifact. Before any capture or dispatch it runs a vision-capability preflight requiring the resolved gate provider/model to advertise image input — surfaced through GateProviderPreflightReport (extend extensions/pi/child-runtime.ts if needed) or the resolved model's input list — failing closed with an actionable remediation naming the configured model when it does not. It then dispatches the visual-gate child through the existing isolated createGateChildSession path with the app and design screenshots attached as images (the amorphic image-attachment path already proven live) and the structured discrepancies plus render-health supplied as text grounding, and parses and validates a strict gate-verdict-v1 with the same hash discipline as the acceptance and safety gates. Currency binds the pixels, not just the JSON: the dispatch hash covers the artifact JSON, the sha256 of each screenshot's exact bytes and its MIME type, and the git base/target tree range, so replacing an image, altering its MIME, or moving the range invalidates the verdict, which is re-verified after dispatch. The runner exposes an injected-invoker seam (like the existing GateModelInvoker) placed AFTER image encoding so the floor exercises the real dispatch envelope with no vision model and no browser; a gate dispatch that errors or times out is a typed fail-closed outcome, never retried as infrastructure. verification-runner.ts stays untouched, so the block still stands.

assertions: the vision-capability preflight fails closed with an actionable remediation naming the configured model when the resolved gate model does not advertise image input, and proceeds when it does — checked before any capture or dispatch, with a stub registry driving both branches

the verdict is currency-bound to the pixels: replacing a screenshot's bytes, altering its MIME, or moving the git tree range after dispatch each invalidates it (one positive control per axis)
a visual-gate dispatch that errors or times out returns a typed fail-closed outcome and is never retried as infrastructure

work_items.title: Lift the block: a visual oracle now passes or fails for real
work_items.summary: Thread capture and the visual gate into verification so a visual oracle runs them after safety, lift the visual-required block only on a genuine pass, and stay fail-closed with a distinct typed reason at every unmet precondition.
work_items.contract: Wire visual acceptance and lift the block. verification-runner gains an OPTIONAL, backwards-compatible lifecycle/process context (a KartaProcessManager owner plus the candidate tree-ish) threaded from its build-finalizer.ts and integration-runner.ts callers, which own the worktree, process owner, and candidate tree; the context-less run() path (karta_dispatch runVerification, and the index.ts construction) has no owner and therefore blocks a visual oracle fail-closed with the typed reason visual-no-context, moving no ref. For a visual oracle, after the safety gate passes and with a context present, the runtime FIRST runs the vision-capability preflight (a no-image-input model blocks visual-no-vision-model with no capture attempted), then runs the pi-visual-capture capture orchestrator over the candidate tree-ish (the staged target tree for a candidate target, the committed OID for committed and merged targets — never a commit OID that does not exist yet) at the design path and app route resolved from the binder's design_facts.source plus the item's existing design_reference work-item field, then the visual-gate runner over the resulting artifact under that same lifecycle owner so servers are reaped on abort. A visual oracle dispatches NO acceptance gate (acceptance stays skipped, as today's visualAcceptancePending path does). Ordered, package-owned derivation: opt-out returns skipped; a non-pass safety verdict surfaces as that safety failure and is never folded into visual; a boundary-only request returns safety alone; then a genuine visual pass returns status pass and LIFTS the block (the item builds, merges, completes) with the verdict recorded in a new gates.visual slot on KartaVerificationResult; concerns returns concerns; every unmet precondition returns blocked with a distinct typed blockedReason and never a silent pass. Widen KartaVerificationBlockedReason from the single visual-required to a closed typed union — visual-no-design (design_reference none, or design_facts.source null or unresolvable), visual-no-env (no visual_env declared), visual-no-vision-model, visual-capture-failed (env-server startup-crash, playwright-cli absent, or an unhealthy/shell render), visual-gate-error, and visual-no-context — all typed, none free-text; the reason field stays reserved for opt-out and spoof-proof. Visual concerns are retryable under the existing acceptance-attempt cap: classify a gates.visual concerns verdict in build-runner.ts's retry classifier so it retries like an acceptance concern, and on cap exhaustion the failed ref is written exactly as capped acceptance/safety concerns write it. Update the visual-required consumers in build-finalizer.ts and integration-runner.ts to hold by default with an actionable message for every visual blockedReason and remove the now-false 'until visual acceptance lands' wording — no fall-through that lets a ref move on a blocked seam. Completion refs (candidate, built, done, accepted, integration) move only on a genuine visual pass; the failed ref moves only on capped visual-concern exhaustion; no ref moves on any blocked prerequisite, which consumes no worker-feedback attempt and survives committed-unmarked and merged-unmarked recovery. Update the pi-visual-capture block-holds tests in place to the conditional behavior, and replace the Pi operator guide's not-accepted-yet section with the accepted behavior and its fail-closed seams.

signals: lifts a shipped fail-closed block — the load-bearing authority change this binder exists for
modifies verification-runner's ordered result derivation and widens a spoof-proof typed union
threads a lifecycle context through build-finalizer, integration-runner, and the retry classifier
the sole item the block-unrun-visual contract authorizes to replace the block
